subject: Catalyst order form - output ownership, training, and feedback license
messages:
From: Michael Hayes <michael@catalyst.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@catalyst.ai>, Legal Team <legal@catalyst.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order form + a couple IP clarifications

Ben / Laura —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our procurement and legal teams reviewed the draft Order Form and sent a marked-up PDF (attached). Two high-level asks we want to resolve quickly so we can move to signature:

1) Output ownership: We need a clear statement that the outputs generated by the Service (responses to our prompts) are owned by Catalyst, and Redwood may not use those outputs for any purpose other than providing the Service back to us.

2) Training & feedback: We are not willing to have our customer data used to train models or for product improvement without explicit opt-in. If Redwood needs telemetry/feedback, it must be aggregated and anonymized, and we need a limited, revocable feedback license.

I've attached the redlines and a short note from Legal. Happy to jump on a call today if helpful — procurement is pushing for signature by end of week.

Best,
Michael
VP Product — Catalyst AI
[attachment: Catalyst_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Hayes <michael@catalyst.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form + a couple IP clarifications

Michael —

Appreciate the clear asks and the PDF. We can take these offline with Legal and Ops. Quick reply to confirm Redwood's starting positions so we set expectations before a call: 

- Outputs: Our standard order form gives customers broad rights to use outputs. We don't claim ownership of customer prompts or outputs. That said, we also need the ability to use outputs transiently to operate and debug the service.

- Training/feedback: Default is opt-out for training on customer data; customers can enable model-learning opt-in in a contract addendum. For telemetry, we typically collect de-identified metrics (latency, token counts, error rates) and use aggregated feedback to improve the service. We can offer a narrower, revocable feedback license.

I'll loop Legal to propose concrete wording. Laura / Markus — can you take the lead on redline suggestions? If you want, I can schedule a 30-min sync with their legal and procurement tomorrow.

Next steps: proposed contract language from Redwood's legal + a short two-column summary of concessions.

Thanks,
Ben
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Hayes <michael@catalyst.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Order form + a couple IP clarifications

Michael / Ben —

Attaching a short summary with proposed redline snippets for the Order Form and MSA. High-level positions below and suggested language snippets: 

1) Output ownership (Order Form, section X):
Proposed: "Customer shall retain all right, title, and interest in and to Customer Content and Outputs (defined as responses generated by the Service in response to Customer Content). Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive license to use Outputs for any lawful purpose. Redwood will not assert ownership of Customer Content or Outputs."

Concessions: Redwood requests a narrow license to use Outputs for debugging and to reproduce incidents, limited to 90 days and solely to provide the Service. 

2) Training & feedback (MSA section Y):
Proposed: "Redwood will not use Customer Content or Outputs to train models for the improvement of Redwood's models or services without Customer's prior written consent. Customer may grant a revocable, limited feedback license permitting Redwood to use anonymized, aggregated outputs and telemetry for the sole purpose of service quality improvements. Such feedback shall not be used to create a model or derivative model trained on Customer Content or Outputs."

3) Audit & escrow: Customer requested auditability for telemetry. We propose a compromise: quarterly telemetry reports and a SOC2+ attestation. For source / model escrow requests, redirect to Dedicated/Private deployment options.

Attachments: redlines_summary.docx (two-column concessions), sample_orderform_snippets.txt

Ben / Markus — please review the snippets. Grace, can you confirm operational feasibility for a 90-day debug window and what we can produce as aggregated telemetry?

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redlines_summary.docx]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Michael Hayes <michael@catalyst.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Order form + a couple IP clarifications

Laura / team —

Operational notes on the suggested language:

- 90-day debug window: feasible. We store ephemeral logs and KV caches for 30-90 days depending on service tier; we can document and standardize the 90-day window for Enterprise deals.

- Anonymized telemetry: we can provide aggregated token usage, latency distributions, error summaries, and feature flags toggles. We will not surface raw prompts or outputs in those reports.

- Training opt-in workflow: engineering can support a contract-flagged opt-in that toggles a customer identifier to allow selective ingestion for model improvement. That toggling will be operational (no automated ingestion without explicit enablement).

I'll prepare a short Ops note with retention windows and data flows to attach to the contract packet.

Grace
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Michael Hayes <michael@catalyst.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@catalyst.ai>, Legal Team <legal@catalyst.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Order form + a couple IP clarifications

Laura / Grace / Ben —

Thanks for the quick responses and the concrete wording — this is much better than the original. Two requests before we send to our execs: 

1) Can you bake the 90-day debug window into the Order Form (not a separate Ops note) and add language that Redwood will provide an incident reproduction package on request (redacted as required) within that period?

2) For the feedback license, add a clause that the license is revocable by written notice and that Redwood will delete any derived telemetry related specifically to our account within 30 days of revocation. 

If you can tweak those two bullets, Procurement will clear and we can route for signature. Call if easier — Michael is available 1–3pm PT.

Best,
Michael
VP Product — Catalyst AI
